GÉANT and the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) A federated European Open Science Cloud can only thrive if researchers can connect, collaborate and access resources seamlessly. GÉANT provides the trusted digital foundations that help make this possible. EOSC is an evolving federation of digital infrastructures and services that enables researchers across Europe to discover, access, share and reuse research data and resources across disciplines and borders. As the pan-European network for research and education, GÉANT plays a key role in supporting this vision. Together with National Research and Education Networks (NRENs) and partners across Europe, GÉANT contributes trusted connectivity, identity and access management, cybersecurity, cloud integration and other core services that underpin a secure and interoperable EOSC Federation. Our involvement extends across a range of European projects that help shape, build and operate EOSC. Through these initiatives, GÉANT contributes technical expertise, community engagement and long-term sustainability, ensuring that researchers benefit from seamless access to the services, data and collaboration opportunities they need to advance science. A pan-European e-infrastructure Node The EOSC Federation is built on trusted Nodes. The GÉANT EOSC Node contributes the connectivity, trust services and expertise that help make federation work. Building on GÉANT’s long-standing expertise in networking, identity and trust services, the Node delivers core capabilities that support interoperability across the EOSC Federation, including authentication and authorisation, secure access, federation services and high-performance connectivity. GÉANT works alongside NRENs and European partners to connect national and thematic EOSC Nodes into a secure, scalable and interoperable ecosystem. For NRENs, the GÉANT EOSC Node also provides a gateway to the EOSC Federation. Organisations that are not yet participating through a national Node can onboard their services via the GÉANT Node as resource providers or use it to connect users with services and resources on demand. The GÉANT EOSC Node builds on a series of major milestones, including the launch of the EOSC EU Node in 2024, the EOSC Federation in 2025 and the EuroHPC Federation Platform in 2026, all contributing to a unified, secure and user-friendly environment for accessing Europe’s research and computing resources. What the GÉANT Node enables The GÉANT Node acts as a gateway between the EOSC Federation and the services, resources and expertise of Europe’s research and education networking community. Here are four examples of how it can make federated access and collaboration a reality. Federated access to EOSC The GÉANT Node will provide the technical solution for the Trust & Identity layer of the EOSC Federation through MyAccessID. It will connect national and institutional identities, enabling secure authentication and Single Sign-On across EOSC Nodes and services. Value to users: Researchers and service providers can use their trusted identities to access EOSC services and resources seamlessly, securely and interoperably. Access to European cloud resources The GÉANT Node will make cloud resources from the OCRE Framework available through the EOSC Federation, connecting researchers and research infrastructures with European cloud providers. Value to users: Easier access to European cloud resources, lowering barriers to cloud adoption while supporting European digital sovereignty. NREN resources through the GÉANT Node The GÉANT Node will act as a gateway for NRENs that are not themselves EOSC Nodes, enabling them to make selected services and resources available through the EOSC Federation. Value to users: A wider range of services and resources becomes accessible through EOSC, while making it easier for NRENs to contribute their capabilities to the Federation. Connecting EOSC and EuroHPC The GÉANT Node will demonstrate how EOSC and EuroHPC can work together through federated identity and Single Sign-On. The use case will connect research data, EOSC services, cloud resources and EuroHPC computing in a seamless research workflow. Value to users: Researchers can move securely between EOSC and EuroHPC resources, enabling data to be processed on European supercomputing infrastructure and the results stored and analysed through EOSC services. GÉANT Service Catalogue In short The GÉANT Node offers network, security, and Identity and Access Management services to the European research community. It enables organisations to establish compliant EOSC Nodes and provides access to services and resources from GÉANT members, including cloud resources, NREN services, AAI federation and links between EOSC and EuroHPC. Related pages EuroHPC HyperConnectivity GÉANT has been awarded a contract by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (JU). Membership The GÉANT Association includes 37 NRENs, NORDUnet, and associates including five Nordic NRENs, KREN, CERN, and ESA. Access granted by GÉANT to the GÉANT Node does not imply that access to Connected Services is granted. Access to Connected Services is granted by the owners of the Connected Services. The clauses of this AUP apply equally to both the GÉANT Node as well as to all Connected Services, from now on collectively referred to as “Services”, as augmented by any specific terms to which adherence will be required during enrolment on any of these Connected Services. Requirements You shall only use the Services in a manner consistent with the policies and for the purposes described above, show consideration towards other users, and collaborate in the resolution of issues arising from your use of the Services. You shall only use the Services for lawful purposes and not breach, attempt to breach, nor circumvent administrative or security controls. You shall respect intellectual property and confidentiality agreements. You shall protect your access credentials (e.g. passwords, private keys or multi-factor tokens); no intentional sharing is permitted. You shall keep your registered information correct and up to date. You shall promptly report known or suspected security breaches, credential compromise, or misuse to the security contact stated below; and report any compromised credentials to the relevant issuing authorities. Reliance on the Services shall only be to the extent specified by any applicable service level agreements listed below. Use without such agreements is at your own risk. Your personal data will be processed in accordance with the privacy statements referenced below. Your use of the Services may be restricted or suspended, for administrative, operational, or security reasons, without prior notice and without compensation. If you violate these rules, you may be liable for the consequences, which may include a report being made to your home organisation or to law enforcement. Revisions to this Acceptable Use Policy GÉANT reserves the right to revise, amend, and/or modify this AUP at any time. Notice of any revision, amendment, and/or modification to this AUP will be posted on the landing page for the GÉANT Node. You agree that your use of the Services, beyond a period of one calendar month after a notice of such change has been provided on the Services for the first time, shall constitute your consent to the revised, amended, and/or modified version of the AUP. Our unique collaboration model delivers an unmatched multiplier effect and creates the digital foundation for research and education in Europe. Does GÉANT work with organisations outside Europe? Yes, through extensive global partnerships, and thanks to funding from the European Commission, GÉANT interconnects over 110 countries worldwide. 05. Where can I find the new GÉANT logo, as well as GÉANT materials and resources? children.main_text: Home . About GÉANT . Vision, mission, strategy Vision, mission, strategy The GÉANT Association provides and advances the digital infrastructure and services required to accelerate research, education, and innovation for a secure and competitive Europe. Membership The GÉANT Association includes 37 NRENs, NORDUnet, and associates including five Nordic NRENs, KREN, CERN, and ESA. Governance The General Assembly is the GÉANT Association’s highest governing body, consisting of representatives from each member. Projects GÉANT projects drive innovation across networking, Identity and Access Management (IAM), global collaboration and more. Vision and mission The GÉANT Association consists of 43 European National Research and Education Networks (NRENs). For decades, we have been building physical and human networks across Europe and around the world. Our unique collaboration model delivers an unmatched multiplier effect and creates the digital foundation for research and education (R&E) in Europe. Together, and as a trusted partner of the European Commission, we power the knowledge sharing and innovation essential for strengthening Europe’s competitiveness, security, and prosperity. Our vision Powering Knowledge for Europe. Our mission The GÉANT Association provides and advances the digital infrastructure and services required to accelerate research, education, and innovation for a secure and competitive Europe. GÉANT Association Strategy 2026-2030 Strategic goals Collaborate to strengthen physical and human networks across Europe and beyond We will further strengthen collaboration between our unique and diverse human network – the most effective way to achieve not just the highest quality and geographic reach of the physical network, but the advancement of the entire digital foundation for research and education. Create scalable, innovative services prioritised by the community We will identify, co-create, and deliver digital services that integrate emerging technology to comprehensively address community priorities, while linking seamlessly to the digital infrastructure we provide. Build a sustainable financial model We will build a sustainable financial model that allows the GÉANT Association to continue its core operations, expand to new markets and end users, realise healthy service and product life cycles, and thrive in a rapidly advancing and commercially competitive technology landscape. Challenges The challenges we face as the GÉANT Association are not static. These are the current primary uncertainties, challenges or risks, and they will be monitored and updated annually: Geopolitical uncertainty with the risk of fragmentation. A diverse association with a spectrum of needs. A highly uncertain funding landscape. A changing EU regulatory environment​. Evolving technology and user expectations. Transformations To both achieve our strategic goals and mitigate challenges, we strive to reach the following transformations by 2030: Realise platforms for NREN collaboration that facilitate both unity and NREN to NREN mutual benefit.​ Ensure organisational and association resilience through a sustainable business and governance model. ​ Establish and execute a common vision on services and innovation with equal access across Europe and globally.​ Leverage our unique position in Europe to increase visibility and influence policy. ​ Mainstream a proactive mindset and approach to anticipate and mitigate future uncertainties. GÉANT Association Strategy Framework 2026-2030 The GÉANT Association Strategy 2026-2030 is underpinned by this Strategy Framework that further elaborates on the strategy and provides the framework for joint execution by the association . It also supports the creation of roadmaps and annual plans which inform the Annual Operating Plan and Budget. Guiding principles The GÉANT Association’s guiding principles provide the foundation for decision making and long term sustainability. They are the lens through which priorities, investments and collaboration models will be assessed. Member centred | Innovation | Scalability | Financial logic | Proactive | Impact Strategic service portfolio The strategic service portfolio is the centrepiece of the GÉANT Association’s future direction. It reflects the association’s commitment to deliver high value, scalable services that meet evolving NREN and R&E user needs while maintaining financial sustainability. It is also diversifying into a complementary set of emerging and professional services to strengthen the human and organisational aspects of the community. Joint design and delivery with NRENs and partners will be reinforced by an effective Product Lifecycle Management system and aligned with an innovation funnel and diversified funding channels. Each of the portfolio areas will ultimately be guided by thematic roadmaps, building on GÉANT’s CTO workshop results where relevant, and each service will have a clear Service Value Statement. Technical services: Network infrastructure | Identity and Access Management (IAM) | Security Emerging services: Data | Education | AI Professional services: Events management | Advisory | Learning and talent development Engagement and partnerships Active engagement and partnerships are what enable and drive GÉANT to build trust, shape policy, expand its reach and co create services with members and partners. As funding opportunities evolve, the GÉANT Association must cultivate a broader and more dynamic partnership model and broaden its ecosystem to integrate new stakeholders from the digital R&E sphere. Engagement is a strategic capability that channels new knowledge, collaborative approaches, donor insights, and a global perspective for R&E service innovation development. Global partnerships The GÉANT Association will maintain and expand strategic partnerships with global Regional Education Networks (RENs) through collaborative projects and mutually beneficial initiatives to extend the value, reach and influence of the GÉANT Association and its members. Influencing and policy engagement The GÉANT Association will be broadly recognised as the secure, trusted, sovereign infrastructure for Europe. Together with its members it will engage proactively with the EC, relevant DGs, and policy bodies to ensure R&E needs remain visible and influential. GÉANT Community Programme The GÉANT Community Programme (GCP) will continue to be led by community representatives and serve as the primary platform for community initiatives. Expanded ecosystem To respond to emerging challenges and opportunities, the GÉANT Association will strengthen and broaden its partnerships and expand its engagement ecosystem where this adds value for NREN members, either directly through services, capabilities or efficiencies, or indirectly through influence, sustainability, scale or future opportunity. Enabling strategies The GÉANT organisation’s Enabling Strategies for Finance and Operation, People and Culture, Partner Relations, Security, and Communications will provide the environment and support needed to build a sustainable financial approach that delivers the strategic service portfolio and ensures effective engagement. Together, these components share common value and goals and help to manage resources. The functions below and accompanying core processes are key enablers of disciplined delivery, financial stability and organisational cohesion. Finance and Operation Project Portfolio and Delivery Service and Product Portfolio Management Compliance and Legal Digital, Data and AI Sustainability People and Culture Partner Relations Security Communications

Procurement and supplier information Procurement and supplier information GÉANT is committed to procurement that is open, competitive, and ethically sound. In this page you'll find the contractual terms governing our supplier relationships, details on how to access our eProcurement portal, and information about our approach to responsible supply chain management. Contact Get in touch, learn more or request support. Formalities Find out more about GÉANT’s official legal and registration details. Commercial Partnership Programme Engage with the largest community of research and education technology providers in Europe. About GÉANT Procurement As a public contracting authority, GÉANT conducts all procurement in accordance with applicable EU public procurement principles, as set out in EU Directive 2014/24/EU, and the Dutch Public Procurement Act (Aanbestedingswet 2012). As an organisation operating across multiple countries and often in the context of EC-funded programmes, we may also be subject to additional requirements arising from European Commission grant agreements. Our procurement is guided by four core principles: Transparency Equal treatment Non-discrimination Proportionality How to work with us We use a range of procurement frameworks and platforms to source the services and expertise we need. If you’re interested in working with GÉANT, the options below are the right place to start. Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for professional services Our DPS for professional services is open to agencies providing temporary personnel. If your organisation supplies contractors or interim professionals, this is how to work with us. Join the DPS for professional services Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for connectivity For suppliers seeking to become approved connectivity providers, our DPS for connectivity covers both subsea and terrestrial services. Subsea connectivity Terrestrial connectivity Official European tendering platform Suppliers are encouraged to subscribe to Tenders Electronic Daily (TED), the official European tendering platform, and create a search option to identify relevant tenders. Explore opportunities on TED Standard Terms for Goods and Services Our standard contractual terms apply to the supply of goods and/or services raised under an approved Purchase Order for values below European Commission (EC) thresholds. All contracts exceeding EC thresholds will compete through a formal procurement exercise or EC-compliant framework and are subject to terms specific to that contract or agreement. GÉANT Terms and Conditions for IT Contracts (PDF) – as modified for IaaS+ Services | OCRE 2024 (January 2025) Our commitment to ethical procurement At GÉANT, we operate with honesty, transparency, and a strong sense of responsibility that extends to our supply chain. We have systems and controls in place to ensure that modern slavery has no place anywhere within our organisation or in any of our supply chains. We invite all our current and future partners to download and read our anti-slavery code of conduct. GÉ​ANT Anti-Slavery Supplier Code of Conduct​​ (PDF) In short Our standard terms cover goods, services, and data processing for all purchase orders, with specific terms available for IaaS+ services via the OCRE 2024 Framework. All tenders are conducted electronically through our Mercell-hosted eProcurement portal . As a responsible and transparent organisation, we also hold all suppliers to our Anti-Slavery Code of Conduct. children.main_text: Home . About GÉANT . Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) Community and collaboration are critical to our success at GÉANT, and gender equality plays a fundamental part in this. Women in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) Explore news stories about inclusivity and gender equality. GÉANT Mentoring Programme (GEM) This initiative supports and develops talent within our community. Contact Get in touch, learn more or request support. We are proud of our diverse community and committed to ensuring that GÉANT remains a positive and supportive workplace and a role model for all. Committee overview To create a truly inclusive work environment, we must consider what barriers exist to gender equality within our organisation and make changes to our activities, policies, and practices, in order to remove them. We must ensure that our workplace culture and ethos respects individual needs and personal circumstances, and enables our employees to enjoy a healthy work-life balance. All employees, no matter what their role, should feel psychologically safe in the work environment. Importantly our leadership team leads by example, showing their commitment to gender equality not just in words but in actions. Striving for gender equality Achieving gender equality is an ongoing process that requires practical steps and continuous evaluation. We recognise that policies alone are not enough; they must be supported by clear actions and measurable outcomes. This includes reviewing how decisions are made, ensuring transparency in recruitment and career progression, and creating a culture where concerns can be raised safely and addressed promptly. By taking these steps, we aim to make progress that is meaningful and sustainable for everyone in our organisation. Gender equality plan Community and collaboration are critical to our success at GÉANT. Gender equality is a fundamental part of this. After considering the potential barriers to gender equality within GÉANT, we created an action plan which, over time, will address the issues identified and help us to become a better organisation. We are proud of our diverse community and committed to ensuring that GÉANT remains a positive and supportive workplace for all, and a role model for our community. Gender Equality Action Plan 2025 (PDF) Gender Equality Plan 2022 (PDF) The GÉANT Gender Equality Plan focuses on four thematic areas: Work-life balance and organisational culture. Gender balance in leadership and decision-making. Gender equality in recruitment and career progression. Measures against gender-based violence, including sexual harassment Gender equality principles The GÉANT Community has developed seven gender equality principles that it wishes organisations involved in the community to endorse. We are inviting each NREN and other affiliated organisations to sign up to and endorse these gender equality principles. By doing so, your organisation is making a commitment to support the principles in all aspects of its operations, and to provide resourcing to organisational and community efforts in order to meet the intentions of these principles. children.title: GÉANT Cloud Frameworks
children.main_text: GÉANT Cloud Frameworks Since 2016, GÉANT’s flagship cloud frameworks have fostered digital transformation across Europe, by enabling easy, convenient, and compliant consumption of commercial cloud services for Research and Education (R&E) institutions. These frameworks - the 2016 IaaS, 2020 IaaS+ (aka OCRE), and now the OCRE 2024 Framework - are developed by the GÉANT community, for the GÉANT community. Together with your country’s NREN Cloud Service Delivery Manager , they allow institutions to procure cloud services fast, efficiently and cost-effectively. The new GÉANT cloud framework – OCRE 2024 – is available as of 3 February 2025 and will be in place for a period of five years. Read more Visit the OCRE 2024 Catalogue Reduced Cost and Complexity The frameworks reduce the cost and complexity of cloud service procurement No institutional tendering is required Significant discounts are available thanks to pan-European aggregation and the economies of scale Advantageous terms and conditions on offer The frameworks are in compliance with all relevant EU Regulations (Procurement, VAT, GDPR etc.). Call-off Contracts with service providers are under local laws and local in-country platform support and call-off is provided as standard. Improved Service Cloud service access is enhanced through peering with service providers at points of presence on the GÉANT pan-European network with significant data ingress/egress waivers in place to reduce costs and improve pricing stability. All platforms support SAML2/OIDC protocol with eduGAIN to improve user accessibility, reduce onboarding costs and complexity and provide assurances for identity and privacy management. The frameworks include not only Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) but also Platform as a Service (PaaS) and Software as a Service (SaaS). Read the Success Stories Enjoy these user stories on OCRE-funded projects: OCRE Success Stories OCRE 2020 Cloud Framework (aka 2020 IaaS+ Framework) The OCRE 2020 Framework (also known as 2020 IaaS+ Framework) lasted from 1 December 2020 until 30 November 2024. It was supported by the OCRE (Open Clouds for Research Environments) project, an EC funded project aiming to provide research and education users easier access to cloud services across Europe. The OCRE 2020 Framework supported 40 European countries with a framework of 473 commercial cloud contracts to ease access and provide volume discounts to research and education institutions. Working in conjunction with members of the GÉANT project, this framework offered substantial benefits to the R&E community. For a list of platforms and service providers that were part of the OCRE 2020 Framework, visit: https://clouds.geant.org/2020iaasplusframeworkproviders Please note: starting from 1 December 2024 it's not possible anymore to contract new Call of Contracts or to sign contract extensions with OCRE 2020 service providers. For information on outstanding call-offs from the previous 2016 IaaS Framework and OCRE 2020 Framework (also known as 2020 IaaS+), please reach out to your local NREN representative or to GÉANT .
